title: Registration and orientation
summary: Orientation is delivered once per session and again after a context restart (SessionStart clear or compact on Claude and Codex, preCompact on Cursor). Each attempt is claimed under a per-session lock, so parallel hooks such as Cursor's concurrent postToolUse deliver it once; an undelivered request settles its claim lost for the next event to repair. Native Windows Cursor Desktop sends startup orientation through beforeSubmitPrompt and can recover on postToolUse. SessionStart registers the session. Picked-project first-turn receipt still requires native Windows QA. On other Cursor Desktop builds a chat without sessionStart can orient through beforeSubmitPrompt. It confirms delivery only after context emission. Each harness writes the exact merged and budgeted context body's UTF-8 byte_count and SHA-256 into the existing delivered marker, without storing the body. Receiving QA reads the marker on its retained host through qa mission host-command, including Cursor where transcripts omit hook bodies. Emission evidence remains distinct from native receiving proof, which waits for released QA. On native Windows, hooks resolve a Cursor Desktop workspace with a slash before its drive letter to the picked project, including for startup orientation. The session record and identity output keep the workspace spelling reported by Cursor. When identity reads harness capabilities on Windows, it uses the native workspace path to look up the manifest. Registration reports registered, exists, skipped with a reason, or refused with a named code. Refusals remain fail-open and surface on stderr and in SessionRegistrationRefused. The authoritative registration write persists the first prompt independently of orientation markers; roster reads hide true probes while an explicit session read returns their audit row marked probe. When the prompt hook never reaches the authority, Stop and SessionEnd on Claude attest the first operator prompt's native timestamp from the session's own transcript (no prompt text) and stamp it write-once on the existing row without registering or reviving it; Cursor SessionEnd verifies a top-level user row and stamps the observed end minus duration_ms. Missing evidence leaves the stamp untouched and emits SessionPromptAttestationSkipped with the reason. Codex declares terminal recovery deferred in its transcript manifest. A retired project's checkout refuses registration as SESSION_PROJECT_RETIRED. A timed-out hook that finishes late carries its stamped age, and a hook observed at or before the row's end reports skipped:stale_replay instead of reviving an ended session or probe.
